content: Purged cross-validation (Lopez de Prado) removes training observations whose label-formation window overlaps a test fold; embargo additionally excludes a post-test window to catch lagged market-reaction leakage. Walk-forward splits are strictly chronological (train always precedes test), so a post-test embargo is redundant there but a pre-test purge horizon still matters at label boundaries. Nested CV adds an inner loop for hyperparameter/module selection entirely within the outer-fold training partition so the outer test fold never informs any selection decision. Combinatorial Purged CV (CPCV) generates multiple train/test path combinations for overfitting diagnostics (PBO).
